acme-eng: Hi @sara_support, after the alpha-2 model swap around 09:13 UTC our webhook consumers began seeing JSON parse errors and a noticeable latency jump (~3x). Sending a minimal repro below.

acme-eng: Request (POST /v1/generate):
```json
{"input":"summarize long invoice text...","mode":"json"}
```

acme-eng: Response we received (streaming, concatenated chunks):
```json
{"items":[{"id":"1","summary":"..."},],}
```

acme-eng: The response above causes our parser to fail with `Unexpected token ]` or `Unexpected token ,` depending on client. Non-streaming responses look fine in our quick checks.

sara_support: Sorry about that — can you share a request_id and the exact model + route you hit? Also roughly what percentage of requests fail and any client SDKs involved? :ear:

acme-eng: request_id=4a7d9f2c, model=redwood/alpha-2, route=/v1/generate. Failures ~30% of calls when output > ~2k chars. Using node-fetch inside our webhook consumer.

marc_engineer: Thanks @acme-eng. That pattern (extra trailing comma before closing array/object) looks like a chunk-boundary concat issue in streaming mode. We did a canary of alpha-2 at 09:12 and promoted to wider canary 09:13 — rolling back to previous build now to confirm. Can you reproduce if you force streaming=false?

acme-eng: Quick test: streaming=false returns valid JSON consistently. So yes, seems isolated to streaming chunk assembly.

deploy-bot: deploy: promoted redwood/alpha-2 to canary by marc_engineer at 2024-11-05T09:13:22Z :rocket:

marc_engineer: Ok, that's useful. We'll instrument the streaming assembly codepath and add additional separators/validation at chunk boundaries. Can you also paste the raw chunk array (i.e., the sequence of chunks you received)? That helps us reproduce boundary sequences.

acme-eng: Pasting a small example of the chunked frames we observed:
```
1: '{"items":[{"id":"1","summary":"First part'
2: ' continued summary"},'
3: '] ,\n'
4: '}'
```

acme-eng: Note chunk 3 contains `] ,` which seems like an extra comma introduced before the final object close.

marc_engineer: That clarifies it — likely a bug where we emit a trailing comma during stream flush when last element boundary aligns with a flush event. We're triaging. Will push a hotfix to the streaming serializer that ensures no trailing commas and add unit tests for boundary cases.

sara_support: Escalating to eng-runtime as P0 for structured-output customers. ETA for initial fix/rollback: 2 hours. We'll follow up with rollback if hotfix could risk other regressions.

acme-eng: Thanks — we're able to pause streaming on our side as a short-term mitigation. Please keep us updated, this is blocking some downstream parsers.

marc_engineer: Understood. I'll post a follow-up once we have a patched build on canary and a reproduction test. If you can keep the failing request_id handy, we'll correlate logs when the patch is live.

acme-eng: request_id=4a7d9f2c (kept). Appreciate the quick response. :pray:

sara_support: Note: creating internal incident ticket #INC-2024-317 and assigning to eng-runtime. Will add timeline and customer impact notes.

marc_engineer: Follow-up: confirmed root cause in streaming serializer; hotfix branch opened, running unit + integration tests. If green we'll roll to canary in ~45min.

acme-eng: Received — we will monitor and report any anomalies after the canary patch.

sara_support: Thanks everyone. We'll update this thread with canary results and rollback decision.
